description: Ask the user one to four multiple-choice questions. Asking doesn't wait for the answers: the call returns at once, the questions stay on the user's screen, and the answers arrive later in a message of their own, whenever the user replies. Use it only for a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you can't settle from the request, the code or a sensible default, such as choosing between approaches or settling an ambiguous requirement. Don't use it for facts you can find out yourself, to ask permission or whether to proceed, or for choices with a conventional default: take the obvious one, say so and go on. Ask everything you need in one call, as the last call of your reply: calls after it in the same reply are not run. Only one set of questions is open at a time; while it is, go on with any work the answers don't decide, and end your turn when nothing is left. The user may see only your questions, not the text before the call, so each must stand alone: give the facts needed to answer it and never refer to "above". Give each question two to four distinct options; put the one you recommend first and end its label with "(Recommended)". The user can always type their own answer, so never add an "Other" option. If the questions stop mattering, or you decide yourself, withdraw them by calling ask_user with withdraw set to true, and say what you decided. Read the answers carefully and follow what they actually say; if the user skipped a question, decide yourself and say what you assumed.

header.description: A short tag shown above the question, at most 12 characters, such as "Database".

multi_select.description: Let the user choose more than one option. Defaults to false.

description.description: What choosing this means, in one sentence.

label.description: The choice, in one to five words.

question.description: The whole question, ending with a question mark.

withdraw.description: Set to true, with no other field, to withdraw your open questions instead of asking: the user no longer sees them.

name: ask_user
